use_when: Reserving a square, correctly sized, correctly coloured box for an icon inside another component — the trailing mark in a Button, the leading mark in a Chip.
dont_use_when: As an icon in its own right. `IconSlot` needs no props at all and draws a complete, plausible arrow, so shipping the placeholder is the path of least resistance and nothing stops it — that is the misuse this component invites. Inside Button and Chip the arrow is the default both ship today; anywhere else pass the real icon from Sunim Icon through `icon`, and give it a name when the mark is the only thing carrying the meaning. As a decorative rule or spacer: it is a slot for meaning-bearing or label-adjacent marks, not a spacing device — reach for a margin token or an `<hr>`. As a way to size an icon a parent already sizes: set the parent's own box instead, because this slot is square and will letterbox anything that is not.
placement: Inside another component, next to a text label. It is not laid out directly on a page.
a11y: Two modes, chosen by whether anything names the slot. `aria-label` names it, and the slot becomes `role="img"` with that name. Without one it is decorative and `aria-hidden`, which is correct beside a label that already says the same thing and is how Button and Chip use it. There is no `label` prop — it used to mean the accessible name here and visible required text on the other three, so it was dropped by ruling and `aria-label`, which is inherited, is the only spelling. `role` and `aria-hidden` stay overridable for a consumer who has a reason this component cannot see. It is never focusable and has no interactive state. Colour is inherited through `--sunim-IconSlot-color` so a consumer on a dark or accent surface can retint it without out-specifying its rules; contrast is therefore the consumer's to meet, not this component's.
